# pcg-ts — agent guide

pcg-ts is a deterministic procedural content generation library for
TypeScript (browser + Node, ESM, package `pcg-ts`, optional three.js
adapter `pcg-ts/three`, optional WebGPU field evaluation `pcg-ts/gpu`).
It combines a domain-based attribute data model
(SoA typed arrays), deferred field expressions, a memoizing node-graph
executor, and a hierarchical streaming runtime. It is designed to be
driven programmatically: node capabilities are enumerable at runtime
(`listNodeTypes()`), graphs round-trip through versioned JSON
(`serializeGraph`/`deserializeGraph`), and all errors are actionable.

## Core mental model

- Data flows through graphs as collections of items: geometry items,
  value items (plain numbers/strings/bools), instances items (transform
  batches for renderers). Items carry tags and a revision id (`rev`).
- A `Geometry` holds four attribute domains: point, vertex, primitive,
  detail (always 1 element), plus topology (vertex->point map, primitive
  vertex ranges). Point-only clouds are the common fast path.
- Attributes are named typed-array columns (f32/i32/u32/bool/string)
  with a tuple size. Standard point attributes: P (f32x3), rot (quat
  f32x4, xyzw), scale (f32x3), density (f32), boundsMin/boundsMax
  (f32x3), color (f32x4), seed (u32).
- A `Field` is a deferred computation resolved per element of a domain.
  Field-capable node params accept a constant OR a field expression;
  scalars broadcast against tuples.
- Cooking pulls from declared graph outputs, topologically, memoizing
  each node on (type, param hash, node seed, input item revs).
  `cook(graph, { outputs: ["name"] })` cooks only the named outputs'
  upstream subgraph; untouched nodes keep their caches, so staged
  pipelines (cook output A, bind data, cook output B) fit in one graph.

## Authoring a graph as JSON

Format (`SerializedGraph`, formatVersion 1 — field names exactly):

- `formatVersion`: 1
- `seed`: number (graph seed; node seeds derive from it)
- `nodes`: [{ `id`: string, `type`: registered type name, `params`: object }]
  Omitted params take their schema defaults. Field-capable params accept
  a field spec object (below) instead of a constant. A `subgraph` node
  additionally carries `subgraph: { graph, inputs, outputs }` — the inner
  graph recursively in this same format plus the exposed pin mappings
  (`{ name, node, pin }` each) — so nested subgraphs round-trip. A
  `dataInput` node serializes with `items: []` (live DataItems are
  runtime-injected; re-bind after deserializing).
- `connections`: [{ `from`: [nodeId, outputPin], `to`: [nodeId, inputPin] }]
- `outputs`: [{ `id`: nodeId, `pin`: outputPin, `name`: result key }]

Complete minimal example (deserializes and cooks as-is):

```json
{
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "seed": 42,
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "scatter", "type": "pointScatterInBounds",
      "params": { "count": 500, "boundsMin": [0, 0, 0], "boundsMax": [50, 0, 50] } },
    { "id": "jitter", "type": "jitterPoints",
      "params": { "amount": { "fn": "fbm", "base": "perlinNoise", "opts": { "frequency": 0.05 } } } }
  ],
  "connections": [ { "from": ["scatter", "out"], "to": ["jitter", "in"] } ],
  "outputs": [ { "id": "jitter", "pin": "out", "name": "points" } ]
}
```

```ts
import { deserializeGraph, serializeGraph, cook, firstGeometry } from "pcg-ts";
const graph = deserializeGraph(json);      // validates everything, names faults
const result = await cook(graph);          // { outputs, stats }
const geo = firstGeometry(result.outputs.points);
serializeGraph(graph);                     // lossless round-trip back to JSON
```

## Authoring a graph in code

```ts
import { Graph, cook, pointScatterInBounds, jitterPoints } from "pcg-ts";
const g = new Graph(42);
const a = g.add(pointScatterInBounds, { count: 500 });
const b = g.add(jitterPoints, { amount: [0.5, 0, 0.5] });
g.connect(a, "out", b, "in");
g.output(b, "out", "points");
const { outputs, stats } = await cook(g); // stats: { cooked, cached, elapsedMs }
```

## Graph mutation and introspection (editor/tooling surface)

Every mutation bumps the graph version; the introspection reads are
frozen snapshots with no mutation path that bypasses version bumps.

- `graph.removeNode(handle)` — removes the node, every connection
  touching it, and every output declared on it (documented cascade); one
  version bump; the removed node's cached outputs are dropped
  immediately. Next cook: former downstream nodes recook, untouched
  branches keep serving their caches. Unknown handles (another graph's,
  or already removed) throw. Removing a subgraph *instance* leaves its
  def and inner graph intact.
- `graph.disconnect(from, "pin", to, "pin")` — removes one matching
  connection, returns `true`. Unknown nodes or pins THROW (naming the
  offender, listing valid pins); a missing connection between valid
  endpoints returns `false` with no version bump. On a `multi` input the
  remaining connections keep insertion order (order is part of
  determinism). Cache contract as removeNode: target and downstream
  recook, untouched branches stay cached.
- `graph.removeOutput(name)` — undeclares a terminal output; the name is
  free to redeclare; unknown names throw, listing declared outputs. Node
  caches untouched (outputs change what a cook pulls, not memo keys), so
  the next cook serves every unchanged node from cache.
- `graph.describe()` — frozen structural snapshot: `{ nodes: [{ id,
  seed, defType }], connections: [{ from: [id, pin], to: [id, pin] }],
  outputs: [{ id, pin, name }] }` in insertion/creation/declaration
  order. `seed` is the derived per-node seed the executor uses; `defType`
  is `undefined` when a def carries no usable type string. Cheap enough
  to call per UI frame. Reports structure verbatim — for a
  subgraph-wrapped graph that includes injected plumbing, which
  serialization excludes.
- `graph.getParams(handle)` — frozen shallow copy of the node's current
  params at call time (later setParam calls not reflected). Nested
  values are live references under the library-wide aliasing rule: treat
  them as frozen, change params only through `setParam`.
- `describeSubgraphPins(def)` — per-instance pins of a `subgraphNode`
  def: frozen `{ inputs, outputs }` of `{ name, kind }` in exposure
  order, kinds resolved live from the recorded spec through nested
  subgraphs. Returns `undefined` for non-subgraph defs; throws
  (GraphValidationError, naming pin and inner node) when later edits
  broke the wrapper.

Mutations keep serialization consistent: `serializeGraph` of a mutated
graph round-trips and cooks identically. Rebuilding via
`deserializeGraph` instead of mutating discards all warm caches.

## Field-expression JSON grammar

A field spec is `{ "fn": <name>, ...args }`. Entries in `args` arrays
may be nested specs, finite numbers, or number arrays (plain values wrap
into `constant`). All 40 fns (`listFieldFns()`):

- Inputs:
  - `{ fn: "constant", value: 1 | [1, 2, 3] }`
  - `{ fn: "attribute", name: "density", tupleSize?: 1 }` (numeric attrs only)
  - `{ fn: "position" }` — reads P (tuple 3); `{ fn: "index" }` — 0,1,2,...
  - `{ fn: "randomField", key?: 0 | "salt" }` — per-element hash random in [0,1)
- Elementwise, `args` with exact arity (scalars broadcast; f64 math, f32 storage):
  - 2 args: `add sub mul div min max lt le gt ge eq dot atan2`
    (comparisons emit 1/0; `dot` reduces tuples to a scalar; `atan2`
    args are [y, x], radians)
  - 1 arg: `abs floor length normalize sin cos tan asin acos atan`
    (trig in radians, elementwise)
  - 3 args: `clamp` (x, lo, hi), `lerp` (a, b, t), `select` (cond, a, b)
  - 5 args: `remap` (x, inMin, inMax, outMin, outMax; unclamped)
- Structure:
  - `{ fn: "vec", args: [x, y, z] }` — 1+ args, concatenates components
  - `{ fn: "component", args: [tupleField], index: 0 }` — extract one component
  - `{ fn: "ramp", args: [scalarField], stops: [[0, 0], [1, 1]] }` —
    piecewise-linear through [position, value] stops, strictly ascending,
    clamped at the ends
- Noise (scalar fields of the sample position; pure function of seed +
  position — the context seed does not affect them):
  - `{ fn: "valueNoise" | "perlinNoise" | "simplexNoise", opts?: {
      seed?: int, frequency?: number, offset?: [x, y, z], position?: spec,
      normalized?: false } }`
    valueNoise in [0,1); perlin/simplex approx [-1,1]
  - `{ fn: "worleyNoise", opts?: { ...same, output?: "f1" | "f2" | "f2-f1",
      exact?: false } }`
    (distance to nearest/2nd-nearest feature point; f1 in [0, ~1.73);
    `exact: true` widens the cell search until provably exhaustive —
    slower, use when the fast approximation's rare artifacts matter)
  - `{ fn: "fbm", base: "perlinNoise" | "valueNoise" | "simplexNoise" | "worleyNoise",
      opts?: { ...same, octaves?: 4, lacunarity?: 2, gain?: 0.5 } }`
    (sum not renormalized: range grows toward base * (1-gain^octaves)/(1-gain))
  - `normalized: true` (any noise, fbm included) affinely remaps the
    documented raw range to exactly [0, 1]. Raw ranges are
    machine-readable: `NOISE_RAW_RANGES` (per noise type) and
    `noiseOutputRange(field)` (per field instance, fbm-aware).

Nested example — density in [0,1] from remapped 4-octave noise:

```json
{ "fn": "clamp", "args": [
    { "fn": "remap", "args": [
        { "fn": "fbm", "base": "perlinNoise", "opts": { "frequency": 0.03, "octaves": 4 } },
        -1, 1, 0, 1 ] },
    0, 1 ] }
```

In code, only fields built by `fieldFromJson(spec)` serialize back via
`fieldToJson`; hand-composed combinator fields cook fine but cannot be
serialized.

## Node types (full schemas: docs/nodes.md, machine-readable: docs/nodes.json)

`listNodeTypes()` entries carry an optional `category` grouping label
(absent when a type declared none); the standard library is fully
categorized: source, sampler, point op, filter, attribute, value,
spawn, io, composite.

- copyToPoints — copy a source cloud onto every target point, composing transforms and seeds
- dataInput — emit externally injected DataItems (`items` set via graph.setParam; serializes as `items: []`, re-bind live data after deserializing)
- filterByAttribute — keep points where a scalar/string attribute passes a comparison
- filterByBounds — keep points inside/outside an axis-aligned box
- filterByDensity — keep points by `density` (threshold or probabilistic)
- jitterPoints — deterministic random offset per point (field-capable amount)
- mergePoints — concatenate point clouds (multi input), union of attributes
- orientAlongVector — write `rot` quaternions so a local axis (default `+z`) follows a field-capable direction (e.g. a tangent/normal attribute), `up` hint fixes roll; zero directions keep their rot
- partitionByAttribute — split into per-value point clouds, tagged `name=value`
- pointGrid — regular grid of points
- pointLine — evenly spaced points on a segment
- pointScatterInBounds — uniform random points in a box
- projectToPlane — orthogonal projection of points onto a plane
- promoteAttribute — move an attribute between domains (first/average/sum/min/max)
- selfPrune — greedy minimum-distance thinning (lowest index wins)
- setAttribute — create/overwrite an attribute from a field-capable value; `type: "string"` picks per element from a `values` list by numeric selector (floor+clamp, total) or writes a constant `stringValue`; optional `seed` param folds into the field evaluation (0 = node seed unchanged)
- setBounds — stamp boundsMin/boundsMax on every point
- spawnInstances — terminal: points to render-agnostic instance batches (4x4 column-major transforms); `assetAttr` names a string attribute for per-point asset ids (empty entries fall back to `assetId`)
- splineSample — arc-length sampling along polyline primitives (emits tangent, curveU)
- subgraph — composite node wrapping an inner graph; create with `subgraphNode(inner, inputs, outputs)` (pins are per-instance), inspect with `getSubgraphSpec` / `describeSubgraphPins`, serializes recursively
- surfaceSample — area-weighted scatter on a triangle mesh with density acceptance (emits normal)
- transferAttribute — transfer an attribute from a `source` geometry onto the input's points; `mapping`: "nearest" (closest source point in 3D, never misses), "uv" (destination point-domain UVs located in the source triangulation's UV space; source UVs read from the vertex domain when present — seam-correct — else point), "raycast" (forward-only ray per point: `direction` or per-point `directionAttr`, nearest hit, optional `maxDistance`). uv/raycast need a triangle source; f32 interpolates barycentrically, i32/u32/bool/string take the dominant corner (largest weight, ties → first corner); shared-edge/equal-distance ties → lowest source primitive index; misses keep the prior value (attribute default if new), count reportable via `missCountAttr` (u32 detail); `attrDomain: "vertex"` reads per-corner source values. Grid acceleration is result-neutral; epsilon policy exported (TRANSFER_BARY_EPS, TRANSFER_AREA_EPS, TRANSFER_DET_EPS, TRANSFER_BOX_PAD_REL)
- transformPoints — per-point translate/rotate/scale, composing with rot/scale attrs (field-capable)
- valueConstant — emit a constant number as a value item
- volumeSample — jittered grid fill of a box or of the input geometry's bounds

## Key invariants and contracts

- Determinism: all randomness derives from seeds via PCG32 + 32-bit hash
  combining. Same graph + seed = byte-identical output across runs,
  platforms, cook orders, and streaming paths. Seed chain: graph seed ->
  node seed = hashCombine(graphSeed, hashString(nodeId)) -> per-point
  hashCombine(seed, index, axis). No Math.random anywhere.
- Purity: node execute treats inputs as immutable and uses only its
  derived seed. The executor memoizes on exactly (type, params, seed,
  input revs); params hash structurally (Fields by their stable key,
  DataItems by rev — geometry is never deep-hashed).
- Cook results are immutable: `CookResult` collections alias live cache
  internals. Clone with `cloneGeometry(geo)` before mutating. Arrays
  bound into params (e.g. dataInput `items`) are captured by reference —
  treat as frozen after binding; bind a fresh array to change data.
- Column lifetime: an evaluated field Column may alias attribute storage
  and is valid only until the geometry is mutated or resized; results
  memoize per EvalContext object, so make a fresh context after mutation.
- Cache invalidation is automatic via memo keys (param edits, seed
  changes, input rev changes, subgraph inner-graph edits). Cancelling a
  cook (AbortSignal -> CookCancelledError) keeps finished nodes' caches.

## World streaming (hierarchical runtime)

`new World({ seed, levels, maxCellsPerLevel?, onCellReady?, onCellEvicted? })`
streams grid cells per level around a viewpoint. Levels are ordered
coarse to fine (optionally one leading unbounded level); each is a
`LevelDef`:

- `name`, `graph`, `bind(graph, ctx)` — required.
- `cellSize`: number (cell edge, world units) or `"unbounded"` (one
  global cell, must be the first level).
- `cellMode?`: `"xz"` (default — square XZ cells, unbounded in Y,
  coords `[cx, cz]`) or `"xyz"` (cube cells, coords `[cx, cy, cz]`,
  radii in full XYZ distance). Nesting: like under like; `"xyz"` under
  `"xz"` uses the containing XZ column as parent; `"xz"` under a
  bounded `"xyz"` parent is rejected at construction; an unbounded
  parent accepts either mode.
- `generationRadius?`: cells cook when their center enters this radius.
  Required (positive) for bounded levels; omit for an unbounded level
  (a value is accepted and ignored there).
- `retainRadius?`: eviction hysteresis, default generationRadius * 1.25.
- `cookOutputs?`: cook only these declared outputs of the graph per
  cell (per-output cooking; names validated at construction). Omit to
  cook all.

Before each cell cook, `bind(graph, ctx)` wires the `CellContext` into
the graph — the only channel for cell data. `ctx` is a discriminated
union on `cellMode`: `{ cellMode, coord, min, max, levelIndex,
levelName, seed, parent? }` with 2D coord/min/max for `"xz"` (and
unbounded) levels, 3D for `"xyz"`. Contract: derive params only from
ctx, and wire `ctx.seed` (= hashCombine(worldSeed, levelIndex,
...coord) — every cell coordinate is hashed) into every stochastic
node. Sanctioned seeding: set seed params per node (vary with
hashCombine(ctx.seed, n); setAttribute's `seed` param folds in as
hashCombine(nodeSeed, seed), 0 = unchanged), or reseed the whole graph
via `graph.setSeed(...)` inside bind — memo keys include seeds and
bind-time writes never count as user edits, so neither causes phantom
recooks. Parent-cell outputs arrive as `ctx.parent.outputs`; inject
them via a dataInput node. `await world.update([x, y, z], { budgetMs?,
signal?, maxCooksPerUpdate? })` cooks nearest-first, evicts by
retainRadius + LRU, and reports { cooked, evicted, pending }.
`world.invalidate(level?, coord?)` forces recooks; parent recooks
cascade staleness to children automatically.

## GPU field evaluation (pcg-ts/gpu)

The serializable field-expression grammar (previous section) is the GPU
surface: every fn compiles to WGSL. A field is GPU-eligible iff it
carries a spec — `getFieldSpec(field)` returns it (only fields built by
`fieldFromJson` do; code-authored fields return undefined and stay on
CPU). One eligible field = one compute dispatch over the whole domain.

Setup (browser):

```ts
import { cook } from "pcg-ts";
import { GpuFieldEvaluator } from "pcg-ts/gpu";
const adapter = await navigator.gpu.requestAdapter();
const device = await adapter.requestDevice();
const gpu = new GpuFieldEvaluator(device, { adapterInfo: adapter.info });
const result = await cook(graph, { gpu });   // CookOptions.gpu
```

Node: `npm i -D webgpu` (Dawn bindings; the library has no dependency
on it), then `const adapter = await create([]).requestAdapter()` with
`import { create } from "webgpu"`.

Surface:

- `GpuFieldResolver` (core interface, no WebGPU types): `{ cacheSalt:
  string; resolveField(field, ctx, stats?): Promise<Column> | null }`.
  `null` is returned synchronously for ineligible fields — the caller
  falls back to the CPU `evaluateField` and the reason is counted. A
  non-null return commits to GPU: it resolves to a freshly allocated
  column (never a view of attribute storage) with the same element type
  and tuple size the CPU would produce; a rejection is an error (device
  failure), never a silent fallback.
- `CookOptions.gpu?: GpuFieldResolver` / `WorldOptions.gpu?` /
  `UpdateOptions.gpu?` (update wins, threaded to every cell cook) /
  `captureAsync(geo, domain, field, seed?, gpu?, stats?)` — the
  graph-free entry point; without `gpu` it is byte-identical to
  `capture`.
- `CookStats.gpu` (present exactly when the cook was given a resolver;
  includes nested subgraph-cook work): `{ dispatches,
  pipelinesCompiled, pipelineCacheHits, fallbacks: Record<reason,
  count> }`. The complete fallback-reason vocabulary:
  - `no-spec` — code-authored field, no serializable spec
  - `compile-error` — spec cannot lower to WGSL against the geometry's
    attribute layout (missing or string attribute, tuple size > 4,
    non-finite f32 constant)
  - `too-many-buffers` — kernel needs > 8 storage buffers (more than 7
    attribute inputs + the output; baseline WebGPU limit)
  - `dispatch-too-large` — element count > 65535 × 64 ≈ 4.19M (baseline
    1D dispatch limit; workgroup size is 64)
- `NodeDef.gpu?: "fields" | "always"` — GPU-adoption marker
  (`setAttribute` is `"fields"`, subgraph defs `"always"`). When a cook
  has a resolver and such a node has a live spec'd Field param, the
  memo key gains `|gpu:<cacheSalt>` — so toggling gpu never serves
  bytes produced by the other path, while nodes without spec'd field
  params keep their cache hits across the toggle. The marker is
  conservative: it applies for spec'd-but-ineligible fields too
  (over-invalidation; bytes stay CPU-identical). `GpuFieldEvaluator`'s
  salt is `"gpu1|<vendor>|<architecture>|<device>|<description>"`
  (format version + adapter identity; missing fields become `?`) —
  bytes from different devices never serve each other.
- Pipelines cache on the evaluator instance (keyed by kernel
  specialization key = codegen version + spec key + attribute layout)
  and persist across cooks; `pipelineCacheSize` getter for tools.
- `compileFieldSpec(spec, { attributes })` and `supportedGpuFieldFns()`
  are exported for direct WGSL inspection; compile errors are
  actionable (they name the spec node and list what is supported).
- World note: toggling gpu between updates does NOT recook stored
  cells (cell staleness is version-based); provenance protects the
  graph memo layer whenever a cell actually recooks.

Determinism contract — the CPU is the bit-exact reference; existing
goldens never move:

- Bit-exact (byte equality): u32 hash/random streams (`randomField`
  with default and string keys, noise lattice hashing), `index`,
  u32/i32 attribute roots, bool→f32 reads, pure hash+compare+select
  trees, and f32 add/sub/mul, clamp/min/max, floor, select/compares.
- On one device, repeated dispatches are run-to-run byte-identical.
- Branchy ops (select, compares, ramp segments, worley cell walks) may
  flip at knife-edge inputs whose operands differ within tolerance.
- Everything else matches within measured budgets. Metric: rangeUlp =
  |cpu−gpu| / (2⁻²³ · max|cpu|) — ULPs at the top of the family's
  output range (raw max-ULP inflates at output zero-crossings, where
  the CPU's f64 interior survives cancellation that f32 cannot).
  Measured on discrete desktop hardware (D3D12/Dawn), 10 000 dense
  hash-derived inputs; budgets are the measured values rounded up
  minimally and may be exceeded on other adapters:

  | family | measured rangeUlp | budget |
  |---|---|---|
  | arith add/sub/mul | 0 | bit-exact |
  | clamp/min/max, floor, select/compare | 0 | bit-exact |
  | div | 0.76 | 1 |
  | lerp | 0.50 | 1 |
  | remap | 0.00 | 1 |
  | ramp (multi-stop) | 1.09 | 2 |
  | dot | 0.70 | 1 |
  | length/normalize (incl. sqrt) | 1.50 | 2 |
  | sin/cos over [−8, 8] | 6.50 | 8 |
  | tan over [−1.45, 1.45] | 19.48 | 24 |
  | asin over [−0.9, 0.9] | 503.99 | 512 |
  | acos over [−0.9, 0.9] | 359.09 | 384 |
  | atan | 67.06 | 80 |
  | atan2 | 64.52 | 80 |
  | valueNoise raw / normalized | 6.53 / 6.53 | 8 / 8 |
  | perlinNoise raw / normalized | 7.69 / 4.21 | 10 / 6 |
  | simplexNoise raw / normalized | 17.46 / 8.55 | 24 / 12 |
  | worley f1 / f2 | 5.16 / 4.71 | 8 / 8 |
  | worley f2−f1 normalized / exact f2−f1 | 9.42 / 9.28 | 12 / 12 |
  | fbm value / perlin / simplex / worley | 4.32 / 4.84 / 19.02 / 4.81 | 6 / 6 / 24 / 6 |
  | composite (ramp∘perlin × (random+attr)) | 9.77 | 12 |

  asin/acos absolute error ≈ 6.7e-5 — the WGSL-specified
  absolute-error class for those builtins.

Out-of-domain inputs are GIGO — measured and documented, not patched:

- min/max with a NaN operand: CPU propagates NaN; a GPU may return the
  non-NaN operand (any adapter must yield NaN or the other operand).
- |v| beyond f32 range: GPU length → Inf and normalize → 0 where the
  CPU's f64 interior survives (≈1.4e20); tiny |v| (≈1.4e-25)
  underflows both to 0 on GPU.
- Noise lattice coords ≥ 2³¹ diverge (JS ToUint32 wraps, WGSL f32→int
  saturates); ordinary lanes stay within the noise budget.
- Subnormal results flush to exactly 0 on GPU; CPU keeps subnormals.

## Errors

Read error messages: they name the offending node id, pin, or param and
list the valid alternatives (e.g. unknown node type errors list all
registered types; unknown field fn errors list all fns; pin errors list
valid pins). Typed classes: GraphValidationError, GraphCycleError,
NodeExecutionError (has .nodeId), CookCancelledError,
GraphSerializationError, FieldJsonError, WorldValidationError.

## Pointers

- README.md — human tour with runnable examples
- docs/nodes.md — full generated node reference (pins, params, defaults, ranges)
- docs/nodes.json — the same registry metadata, machine-readable
- docs/authoring.md — graph JSON spec, complete field grammar, recipes,
  GPU eligibility rules
- examples/ — eight vite demos; 06-graph-editor is an interactive node
  editor built on this same registry metadata and JSON format;
  08-gpu-fields cooks the same graph on CPU and GPU with a live parity
  readout
